pr_title: Raise when using key which can't respond to `#to_sym` in EncryptedConfiguration
pr_body:
As is the case when trying to use an integer as a key, which is unsupported.

This replaces the following less-friendly error:

```
NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for an instance of Integer
    lib/active_support/ordered_options.rb:38:in 'ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions#[]='
    lib/active_support/delegation.rb:167:in 'Kernel#public_send'
    lib/active_support/delegation.rb:167:in 'ActiveSupport::EncryptedConfiguration#method_missing'
```

With a more helpful error message:

```
ActiveSupport::EncryptedConfiguration::InvalidKeyError: Key '42' is invalid, it must respond to '#to_sym' from configuration in '/tmp/config-20240530-4153925-tfzzt/credentials.yml.enc'.
    lib/active_support/encrypted_configuration.rb:99:in 'block in ActiveSupport::EncryptedConfiguration#deep_symbolize_keys'
    lib/active_support/core_ext/hash/keys.rb:120:in 'block in Hash#_deep_transform_keys_in_object'
    lib/active_support/core_ext/hash/keys.rb:119:in 'Hash#each'
    lib/active_support/core_ext/hash/keys.rb:119:in 'Enumerable#each_with_object'
    lib/active_support/core_ext/hash/keys.rb:119:in 'Hash#_deep_transform_keys_in_object'
    lib/active_support/core_ext/hash/keys.rb:66:in 'Hash#deep_transform_keys'
    lib/active_support/encrypted_configuration.rb:96:in 'ActiveSupport::EncryptedConfiguration#deep_symbolize_keys'
    lib/active_support/encrypted_configuration.rb:86:in 'ActiveSupport::EncryptedConfiguration#config'
```

Fixes: #51215

issue_context.title: Fix supporting encrypted configuration with integer keys
issue_context.body:
We should accept hashes with integer keys when deep transforming encrypted configuration. Example:

```
{1 => 1}
```

Before https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42358 :

```
> deep_transform(hash)

{1=>1}
```

After https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42358 :

```
> deep_transform(hash)

ruby/gems/3.3.0/gems/activesupport-7.1.3.2/lib/active_support/ordered_options.rb:38:in `[]=': undefined method `to_sym' for an instance of Integer (NoMethodError)

      super(key.to_sym, value)
               ^^^^^^^
Did you mean?  to_s

```

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
7.1.3.2

**Ruby version**:
3.0.2
comments: When does an integer as credential name makes sense?

Thanks for asking, Rafael.

Following is a real use case from one of my applications (using fake credentials), in which I have a "year => spreadsheet ID" mapping.

```
google:
  credentials: config/credentials/google/development.json
  spreadsheet_id:
    2021: 81ab723369a5f16cb68d22f67089b4754befbb32a91b
    2022: ede01aa536d886affa5a4795ff76766413f1a5b062f0
    2023: e0b894384abdcbfb7549ab23907435668f7b48c7ff12
    2024: a59545b56a896e821dcf8b8e6315a68c412bbbff531c
```

With that in place I've been used to do this for a long time:

```
Rails.application.credentials[:google][:spreadsheet_id][month.year]
```

Without accepting integer keys, I have to worry about parsing month.year to string (for example), which is not the behavior I would expect from a hash.

This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not been commented on for at least three months.
The resources of the Rails team are limited, and so we are asking for your help.
If you can still reproduce this error on the `7-2-stable` branch or on `main`, please reply with all of the information you have about it in order to keep the issue open.
Thank you for all your contributions.

I looked into this, and came to the conclusion that this is just not supported.

See this branch as an example of why: https://github.com/rails/rails/compare/main...zzak:rails:51215

Basically, encrypted config uses [OrderedOptions](https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/OrderedOptions.html) under the hood, it is designed to support method call syntax for digging into the hash.

The examples for [EncryptedConfiguration](https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/EncryptedConfiguration.html) demonstrate this.

However, in Ruby integers are now able to be used for method definitions or calls.

```
syntax error, unexpected integer literal (SyntaxError)
def 1
    ^
```

This also doesn't work:

```
Thing.42
```

Since Encrypted Configuration is intended to support dynamic method lookup, we cannot have it both ways.
In other words, I don't think this a bug.

If you can think of a way to support your use-case without breaking backwards compatibility please open a PR.

Thanks for your time looking into this, @zzak.

If there's no way to support this use-case, perhaps we should update [EncryptedConfiguration](https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/EncryptedConfiguration.html) documentation accordingly, as it currently states that

> Values can be accessed via Hash methods, such as fetch and dig

Based on that it should accept integer keys too.

Also we can take this example from documentation:

> my_config.fetch(:foo)

From which we can infer that we can do this as well:

> my_config.fetch(1)

Which is acceptable by Ruby Hash:

```
$> {1 => 2}.fetch(1)
=> 2
```

@fabianof I don't think it's good API design to only allow certain methods be supported like this, and I've started working on a PR to raise an error pointing to the affected key in your case.

As a workaround, you can use string keys, and still access your data through `fetch` or `[]` but the method lookup syntax will not work (the Ruby interpreter will raise a syntax error, which is the best case scenario imo).

review_comments: @zzak @eileencodes it looks like this call to Hash#deep_symbolize_keys is not doing anything useful here and should be removed. Right?
Whoops, yeah. Good catch. Do you want to open a PR? :pray:
